1.subtopic: Band Theory, Doping, and Semiconductor Types
1.solution:
An n-type semiconductor is made by doping with pentavalent (donor) atoms such as phosphorus, which supply extra electrons.
Electrons are the majority carriers and holes are the minority carriers.
Hence: holes are minority carriers and pentavalent atoms are dopants.

2.subtopic: Self-Inductance, Energy Stored, and LR Circuit
2.solution:
Change in current \(\Delta I = 5-(-5)=10\,\text{A}\).
\(e = L\dfrac{\Delta I}{\Delta t}\Rightarrow L=\dfrac{e\,\Delta t}{\Delta I}=\dfrac{2\times0.5}{10}=0.1\,\text{H}=100\,\text{mH}\).

3.solution: Just outside a charged conductor, the field is \(E=\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\) and is directed normal (perpendicular) to the surface.

4.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
4.solution:
Excess pressure in a soap bubble \(P=\dfrac{4T}{r}\), so \(P\propto\dfrac{1}{r}\).
\(P_1=3P_2\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{r_1}=\dfrac{3}{r_2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{r_1}{r_2}=\dfrac{1}{3}\).
\(\dfrac{V_1}{V_2}=\left(\dfrac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^3=\dfrac{1}{27}\).

5.subtopic: Progressive Wave, Wave Equation, and Velocity
5.solution:
Maximum particle velocity \(v=A\omega\), with \(\omega=\dfrac{2\pi V}{\lambda}\) (where \(V\) is the wave speed).
Thus \(v=A\cdot\dfrac{2\pi V}{\lambda}=\dfrac{2\pi A}{\lambda}V\).

6.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
6.solution:
For the hanging mass \(M\) to stay stationary, the tension equals its weight: \(T=Mg\).
This tension provides the centripetal force for \(m\): \(mr\omega^2=Mg\), with \(r=L\).
\(\omega^2=\dfrac{Mg}{mL}\Rightarrow (2\pi f)^2=\dfrac{Mg}{mL}\Rightarrow f=\dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{Mg}{mL}}\).

7.solution:
For a regular hexagon, the distance from the centre to each vertex equals the side \(=6\,\text{cm}=6\times10^{-2}\,\text{m}\).
\(V_0=6\times\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q}{r}=6\times9\times10^{9}\times\dfrac{2\times10^{-6}}{6\times10^{-2}}=1.8\times10^{6}\,\text{V}\).

8.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
8.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
8.solution:
Stopping potential: \(V_0=\dfrac{h}{e}f-\dfrac{\phi}{e}\), a straight line with slope \(\dfrac{h}{e}\).
The slope depends only on \(h\) and \(e\), not on the work function, so the ratio of slopes is \(1:1\).

9.subtopic: Newton's Laws — Force, Tension, Lift, and Connected Blocks
9.solution:
Stationary lift: \(W_1=mg\). Lift moving down with acceleration \(a\): \(W_2=m(g-a)\).
\(\dfrac{W_1}{W_2}=\dfrac{g}{g-a}=\dfrac{4}{3}\Rightarrow 3g=4g-4a\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{g}{4}\).

10.solution:
\(N=N_0e^{-\lambda t}\). At \(t=3\): \(\dfrac{N_0}{e}=N_0e^{-3\lambda}\Rightarrow \lambda=\dfrac{1}{3}\,\text{min}^{-1}\).
Half value: \(\dfrac{N_0}{2}=N_0e^{-\lambda t}\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\ln 2}{\lambda}=3\log_e 2\) minutes.

11.solution:
For a stretched wire \(n\propto\sqrt{T}\), so beat frequency \(=\left|\sqrt{T_1}-\sqrt{T_2}\right|=6\), with \(T_1>T_2\).
To keep the difference (and hence beats) unchanged, the gap \(\sqrt{T_1}-\sqrt{T_2}\) must be preserved — achieved by decreasing \(T_1\) or increasing \(T_2\).

12.subtopic: Gas Laws and Ideal Gas Equation
12.solution:
Isothermal: \(P_1V_1=P_2V_2\). Volume reduced by 5%: \(V_2=\dfrac{19}{20}V_1\).
\(P_2=\dfrac{20}{19}P_1\Rightarrow P_2-P_1=\dfrac{P_1}{19}=0.0526\,P_1\), i.e. an increase of \(5.26\%\).

13.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference

14.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
14.subtopic: Force on Current-Carrying Conductor and Parallel Wires
14.solution:
Forces on the two sides parallel to the wire act; the perpendicular sides cancel.
Near side AB at \(\dfrac{L}{3}\): \(F_{AB}=\dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi(L/3)}L=\dfrac{3\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi}\).
Far side CD at \(\dfrac{4L}{3}\): \(F_{CD}=\dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi(4L/3)}L=\dfrac{3\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{8\pi}\).
\(F_{net}=F_{AB}-F_{CD}=\dfrac{9\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{8\pi}\).

15.subtopic: Transistors — BJT, CE Amplifier, and Gain

16.subtopic: Prism — Deviation, Dispersion, and Refractive Index
16.solution:
Emergent ray grazes the second face, so \(e=90^\circ\).
\(\mu=\dfrac{\sin e}{\sin r_2}=\dfrac{1}{\sin r_2}=\sqrt{2}\Rightarrow \sin r_2=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\Rightarrow r_2=45^\circ\).
For an equilateral prism \(A=60^\circ\), so \(r_1=A-r_2=15^\circ\).
\(\sin i=\mu\sin r_1=\sqrt2\sin15^\circ\Rightarrow i=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\sqrt2\sin15^\circ\right)\).

18.subtopic: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws — Induced EMF, Current, and Charge
18.solution:
As the magnet's north pole moves away, the flux through the loop decreases.
By Lenz's law the induced current opposes this decrease, driving current from \(a\) to \(b\) through the connecting wire, so positive charge accumulates on plate \(b\).

19.subtopic: Doppler Effect — Moving Source and Observer
19.solution:
Observer moving towards stationary source: \(n'=\left(\dfrac{v+v_o}{v}\right)n\), with \(v_o=\dfrac{v}{5}\).
\(n'=\dfrac{6}{5}n\Rightarrow n'-n=\dfrac{1}{5}n=20\%\) of \(n\).

20.subtopic: Reactance — Inductive, Capacitive, and Single-Element Circuits
20.solution: In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current lags the e.m.f. by \(90^\circ\). The graph showing the current lagging the e.m.f. by a quarter cycle (figure B) is correct.
20.note: Four-image 'which graph' stem: imageRefs are the four candidate phasor/waveform graphs labelled (A)-(D). The option texts map to these figures; AK keys figure (B). optionFigures not set because options carry text labels referencing the figures, not the images themselves.

21.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
21.solution:
Surface-tension force acts along each line of contact. The disc with a hole has an outer edge (length \(2\pi R\)) and an inner edge (length \(2\pi r\)).
Total force \(=T(2\pi R)+T(2\pi r)=2\pi T(R+r)\).

22.solution:
For a sonometer \(f\propto\dfrac{1}{l}\), so \(f_1l_1=f_2l_2\Rightarrow 23f_1=24f_2\) (shorter length gives higher frequency).
Also \(f_1-f_2=4\). Solving: \(f_1=96\,\text{Hz},\ f_2=92\,\text{Hz}\).

23.solution:
Brewster's law: \(n=\tan i_p=\dfrac{C}{V}\).
\(\dfrac{\sin i_p}{\cos i_p}=\dfrac{C}{V}\Rightarrow V\sin i_p=C\cos i_p\).

24.solution:
No current in the 5\(\,\Omega\) galvanometer arm \(\Rightarrow\) balanced Wheatstone bridge. The two outer paths are in parallel.
\(R_1=10+15=25\,\Omega\), \(R_2=20+30=50\,\Omega\).
\(R=\dfrac{25\times50}{75}=16.67\,\Omega\approx17\,\Omega\).

25.subtopic: Transistors — BJT, CE Amplifier, and Gain

26.solution:
Random errors are unpredictable fluctuations. Improper calibration and zero error are systematic; a single misreading is a gross/personal error.
Errors from fluctuations in the electric power supply are random.

27.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
27.subtopic: de Broglie Wavelength and Matter Waves
27.solution:
\(\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}\Rightarrow E\propto\dfrac{1}{\lambda^2}\).
Halving \(\lambda\): \(\dfrac{E_2}{E_1}=\left(\dfrac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}\right)^2=4\Rightarrow E_2=4E_1\).
Energy added \(\Delta E=3E_1\Rightarrow n=3\).

28.subtopic: Reactance — Inductive, Capacitive, and Single-Element Circuits
28.solution:
For a pure capacitor with \(E=E_0\sin\omega t\), current leads voltage by \(90^\circ\) and \(I_0=\dfrac{E_0}{X_C}=E_0\omega C\).
\(I=E_0\omega C\sin\!\left(\omega t+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\).

29.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
29.solution:
For banking, \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{V^2}{Rg}\) and \(\tan\theta\approx\dfrac{h}{b}\) (since \(b\gg h\)).
\(\dfrac{h}{b}=\dfrac{V^2}{Rg}\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{V^2 b}{Rg}\).

30.subtopic: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, and Isochoric Processes

31.subtopic: SHM Energy — Kinetic, Potential, and Total

32.solution:
A conducting slab of thickness \(t\) reduces the effective gap to \(d-t\).
Here \(t=\dfrac{2d}{3}\Rightarrow d'=\dfrac{d}{3}\).
\(C_1=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d/3}=\dfrac{3\varepsilon_0 A}{d}=3C\Rightarrow \dfrac{C_1}{C}=\dfrac{3}{1}\).

33.subtopic: Newton's Law of Gravitation and Gravitational Force
33.solution:
Total enclosed mass beyond \(2r\) is \(2m\). At \(x=2.5r\) (outside both): \(g=\dfrac{G(2m)}{(2.5r)^2}=\dfrac{2Gm}{6.25r^2}=\dfrac{8}{25}\dfrac{Gm}{r^2}\).
Option B matches; the others give wrong values (at 15r it is \(\tfrac{2}{225}\tfrac{Gm}{r^2}\); at 1.5r it is non-zero; the region between is not uniform).

34.solution:
Primary power \(P=I_pV_p=5\times220=1100\,\text{W}\).
With 50% loss, secondary power \(=550\,\text{W}\).
\(I_s=\dfrac{P_s}{V_s}=\dfrac{550}{2200}=0.25\,\text{A}\).

35.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
35.subtopic: Magnetic Moment of Current Loop and Galvanometer Instruments
35.solution:
\(A=\pi r^2\Rightarrow r=\sqrt{\dfrac{A}{\pi}}\). \(B=\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2r}\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{2B}{\mu_0}\sqrt{\dfrac{A}{\pi}}\).
Magnetic moment \(M=IA=\dfrac{2B}{\mu_0}\sqrt{\dfrac{A}{\pi}}\cdot A=\dfrac{2BA^{3/2}}{\mu_0\sqrt{\pi}}\).

36.solution:
Open pipe: \(n_1=\dfrac{V}{2L}\). With \(\dfrac{3}{4}\) of the length in water, the air column \(=\dfrac{L}{4}\) and acts as a closed pipe.
\(n_2=\dfrac{V}{4(L/4)}=\dfrac{V}{L}\).
\(\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}=\dfrac{V/2L}{V/L}=\dfrac{1}{2}\).

38.subtopic: Gas Laws and Ideal Gas Equation
38.solution:
\(PV=Nk_BT\). Jar A: \(PV=N_1k_BT\). Jar B: \((2P)\dfrac{V}{4}=N_2k_B\dfrac{T}{4}\Rightarrow PV=\dfrac{N_2k_BT}{2}\).
Equating: \(N_1=\dfrac{N_2}{2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{N_1}{N_2}=\dfrac{1}{2}\).

39.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
39.solution:
Orbital period \(t=\dfrac{2\pi r}{v}\). Current \(I=\dfrac{e}{t}=\dfrac{ev}{2\pi r}\).
Rearranging: \(\dfrac{r}{v}=\dfrac{e}{2\pi I}\).

40.subtopic: Series LCR — Impedance, Phase, and Resonance
40.solution:
Inductors \(L\) and \(2L\) in series: \(L_{eq}=3L\). Capacitors \(C\) and \(2C\) in parallel: \(C_{eq}=3C\).
\(f=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{L_{eq}C_{eq}}}=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{9LC}}=\dfrac{1}{6\pi\sqrt{LC}}\).

41.solution:
From the figure, \(q_1\) and \(q_2\) are adjacent corners (separation \(a\)), \(q_1\) and \(q_3\) are diagonal corners (separation \(\sqrt2\,a\)).
\(F_{12}=\dfrac{kq^2}{a^2}\), \(F_{13}=\dfrac{kq^2}{2a^2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{F_{13}}{F_{12}}=\dfrac{1}{2}\).

42.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
42.solution:
Centripetal acceleration \(a=\omega^2 r\). Same period \(\Rightarrow\) same \(\omega\), so \(a\propto r\).
\(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2}=\dfrac{R}{r}\).

44.subtopic: SHM Kinematics — Displacement, Velocity, Phase, and Damping
44.solution:
Damped amplitude \(A=A_0e^{-\lambda t}\). In 2 s it becomes \(\dfrac{1}{3}\): \(e^{-2\lambda}=\dfrac{1}{3}\).
In 6 s: \(e^{-6\lambda}=(e^{-2\lambda})^3=\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^3=\dfrac{1}{27}\Rightarrow n=27\).

45.solution:
Two identical branches (each: 3 V cell with 3\(\,\Omega\)) feed the common 6\(\,\Omega\). Let branch currents be \(I_1,I_2\).
Loop equations: \(9I_1+6I_2=3\) and \(6I_1+9I_2=3\Rightarrow I_1=I_2=\dfrac{1}{5}\,\text{A}\).
Current through 6\(\,\Omega\): \(I_1+I_2=\dfrac{2}{5}\,\text{A}\).

47.solution:
Through first polaroid: \(I_1=\dfrac{I_0}{2}\). Through second at \(30^\circ\): \(I_2=I_1\cos^2 30^\circ=\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cdot\dfrac{3}{4}=\dfrac{3I_0}{8}\).
Fraction transmitted \(=\dfrac{3}{8}=37.5\%\).

48.subtopic: Kinematics — Equations of Motion, Free Fall, and Graphs
48.solution:
Change in velocity = area under the a-t graph. The graph is a triangle with peak \(8\,\text{m/s}^2\) at \(t=0\) falling to zero at \(t=10\,\text{s}\).
\(\Delta v=\dfrac{1}{2}\times10\times8=40\,\text{m/s}\). Starting from rest, \(v_{max}=40\,\text{m/s}\).

51.solution:
A salt of a weak acid and a strong base hydrolyses to give a basic solution.
\(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\) is the salt of weak acid \(\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\) and strong base NaOH, so the carbonate ion hydrolyses making the solution basic.
\(\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3\) and \(\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}\) are acidic; \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\) is neutral.

52.solution:
1,2-Dibromoethane with alcoholic KOH undergoes double dehydrohalogenation in two steps.
First elimination gives vinyl bromide (A), and a second elimination (with sodamide \(\text{NaNH}_2\)) removes the second HBr to give ethyne (B).
\(\text{BrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2{=}\text{CHBr} \rightarrow \text{HC}{\equiv}\text{CH}\)

53.subtopic: Preparation Methods of Aldehydes and Ketones
53.solution:
The conversion shown is a gem-dihalide (or an acetal/ozonide-type intermediate) being hydrolysed; the reagent that brings the indicated conversion to the carbonyl compound is water.
\(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) (hydrolysis) furnishes the product, so R = \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\).

54.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy
54.solution:
An exothermic process releases heat.
The neutralisation of strong base KOH with strong acid \(\text{HNO}_3\) gives salt and water with release of heat, hence exothermic.
Melting of ice and dissolution of NaCl are endothermic; \(\text{N}_2 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2\) is endothermic (positive \(\Delta H_f\)).

55.solution:
For fcc, number of atoms per unit cell \(n = 4\).
Number of atoms in mass \(x\) g \(= \dfrac{x\,n}{\rho a^3}\).
For 1 g: \(\dfrac{1 \times 4}{1.728 \times 10^{-22}} = 2.315 \times 10^{22}\) atoms.

56.solution:
In the spectrochemical series, ligand field strength increases as:
\(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} < \text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{OH}^- ...\ < \text{CN}^- < \text{CO}\).
CO is the strongest field ligand among the given options.

57.solution:
Reduction of nitroethane to ethylamine with Sn/HCl:
\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2 + 6[\text{H}] \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\).
Six hydrogen atoms (6 H\(^+\) + 6 e\(^-\)) are required per mole.

58.subtopic: Rate of Reaction, Stoichiometry and Average Rate

59.subtopic: Balancing Redox Reactions and Oxidized/Reduced Species
59.solution:
In \(\text{Ag}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Ag} + 2\text{OH}^-\), silver goes from +1 to 0 (gain of electrons).
This is a reduction half-reaction, so silver is reduced.

60.solution:
Liquid helium is used to cool the superconducting magnets in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machines.
Hence He is the inert gas used.

61.subtopic: Ionic Equilibrium, Ka, Kb and Degree of Dissociation
61.solution:
Degree of dissociation \(\alpha = 5\% = 5 \times 10^{-2}\), concentration \(c = 0.01\,\text{M}\).
Dissociation constant \(K = \alpha^2 c = (5 \times 10^{-2})^2 \times 0.01\)
\(= 2.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.01 = 2.5 \times 10^{-5}\).

62.solution:
Markovnikov addition of HBr places Br on the more substituted carbon of the double bond.
To obtain 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane (Br and CH3 on the same carbon), the methyl group must sit on a double-bond carbon, i.e. 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene.
HBr then adds H to C2 and Br to C1 (which bears CH3), giving the tertiary bromide.
Option A (1-methylcyclohexene) is the correct alkene.
62.note: Figure question — options A-D are structures (image16-image19). Read images: A = 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene (CH3 on double-bond C), B = 3-methylcyclohexene, C = 4-methylcyclohexene, D = methyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene. Only A gives 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane by Markovnikov HBr addition.

63.subtopic: Preparation Methods of Aldehydes and Ketones
63.solution:
Acid chlorides react with dialkylcadmium to give ketones.
\(2\,\text{CH}_3\text{COCl} + (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{Cd} \rightarrow 2\,\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CdCl}_2\)
The substrate S giving propanone (and cadmium chloride) is ethanoyl chloride (acetyl chloride).

64.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work

65.solution:
A bcc unit cell has a packing efficiency of 0.68 (68%).
Volume occupied by particles \(= 0.68 \times\) volume of unit cell
\(= 0.68 \times 8.0 \times 10^{-23} = 5.44 \times 10^{-23}\,\text{cm}^3\).
65.stemOverride: Calculate the volume occupied by all particles in bcc unit cell if the volume of unit cell is \(8.0 \times 10^{-23}\,\text{cm}^3\).

66.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
66.solution:
In hexacyanoferrate(II), \([\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}\): Fe atomic number Z = 26, Fe is +2 (loses 2 e\(^-\)), 6 CN\(^-\) ligands donate \(6 \times 2 = 12\) electrons.
EAN \(= 26 - 2 + 12 = 36\).

67.subtopic: Nucleic Acids, DNA, RNA, Nucleotides and Bases
67.solution:
A ribonucleoside = ribose sugar + nitrogenous base (no phosphate).
Ribose contributes the 2'-OH, 3'-OH and 5'-OH groups, giving a total of 3 -OH groups in a ribonucleoside.

68.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life
68.stemOverride: The rate constant of a first order reaction is \(1.15 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{s}^{-1}\). How long will 5 g of reactant take to reduce to 3 g?

69.subtopic: Group 1 Alkali Metals, Properties and Reactivity
69.solution:
Sodium burns in excess oxygen to form sodium peroxide:
\(2\text{Na} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{O}_2\).
Carbon gives oxides (CO/CO2), and the noble gases Ar and He do not react with oxygen.

70.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
70.solution:
In the cell \(A_{(s)}|A^{2+}\,\|\,B^+|B_{(s)}\), A is the anode (oxidation) and B is the cathode (reduction).
Balancing electrons (A gives 2 e\(^-\), each B\(^+\) takes 1 e\(^-\)):
\(A_{(s)} + 2B^+_{(aq)} \rightarrow A^{2+}_{(aq)} + 2B_{(s)}\).

71.solution:
For a binary salt AB: \(K_{sp} = S^2\).
Molar solubility \(S = \dfrac{1.12 \times 10^{-4}}{112} = 1.0 \times 10^{-6}\,\text{mol dm}^{-3}\).
\(K_{sp} = (1.0 \times 10^{-6})^2 = 1 \times 10^{-12}\).
71.stemOverride: Solubility of binary sparingly soluble salt is \(1.12 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{g/dm}^3\). Calculate its solubility product (molar mass of salt = 112 g mol\(^{-1}\))

72.subtopic: Preparation of Alkanes, Wurtz, Grignard and Decarboxylation
72.solution:
Ethanol \(\xrightarrow{\text{SOCl}_2}\) ethyl chloride (X) \(\xrightarrow{\text{Mg/dry ether}}\) ethylmagnesium chloride (Y).
Hydrolysis of the Grignard reagent (with water) gives ethane (Z).
\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + \text{Mg(OH)Cl}\).

73.subtopic: Physical Properties of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
73.solution:
Water solubility is governed by hydrogen bonding with water.
Phenol forms strong H-bonds with water and has no bulky hydrophobic substituent.
p-Cresol (extra CH3) and the nitrophenols (larger, with internal/intramolecular interactions) are less soluble, so phenol is most soluble.

74.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy

75.subtopic: Van't Hoff Factor and Abnormal Molar Mass
75.solution:
Urea is a non-electrolyte (i = 1): \(\Delta T_f = K_f m = x\,\text{K}\).
\(\text{CaCl}_2\) dissociates into 3 ions (i = 3) at the same molality:
\(\Delta T_f = i K_f m = 3 \times (x) = 3x\,\text{K}\).

76.solution: Eugenol (4-allyl-2-methoxyphenol, from clove oil) is well known for its analgesic and antimicrobial (and local anaesthetic) properties, widely used in dentistry.

77.subtopic: Glycosidic Linkages in Di- and Polysaccharides
77.solution: Cellulose is a linear polymer of \(\beta\)-D-glucose units joined by \(\beta\)-1,4-glycosidic linkages.

78.subtopic: Colour, Magnetic Properties and Spin-Only Formula
78.solution:
\(\text{Zn}^{2+}\) is \([\text{Ar}]3d^{10}\) with no unpaired electrons (n = 0).
Spin-only moment \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{0} = 0\) BM (diamagnetic).

79.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
79.solution:
Multimolecular colloids form by aggregation of a large number of small atoms/molecules.
Sulphur sol consists of aggregates of \(\text{S}_8\) molecules, a classic multimolecular colloid.
Starch and cellulose are macromolecular colloids.

80.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
80.solution:
Electrode potential is an intensive property — it does not change when the equation is multiplied.
Reversing the reduction (E\(^\circ\) = +0.34 V) gives the oxidation potential E\(^\circ\) = -0.34 V, and this value is unchanged for 2 Cu atoms.

81.subtopic: Real Gases, Dalton's Law and KTG
81.solution:
For equal masses, moles \(\propto 1/M\); partial pressure \(\propto\) mole fraction \(\propto\) moles.
\(\text{H}_2\) has the smallest molar mass (2 g/mol), so the greatest number of moles and the maximum partial pressure.

82.solution:
Reaction of aryl halide with sodium in dry ether to give biphenyl is the Fittig reaction.
\(2\,\text{Ar–Br} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Ar–Ar} + 2\text{NaBr}\).

83.solution:
Vapours of phenol with hydrogen over a Ni catalyst at 433 K undergo ring hydrogenation to give cyclohexanol.
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 3\text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni, 433 K}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{OH}\) (cyclohexanol).

84.solution:
Angular momentum \(mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}\); for the first orbit n = 1.
\(= \dfrac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{2 \times 3.14} = 1.05 \times 10^{-34}\,\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}\).

85.subtopic: Van't Hoff Factor and Abnormal Molar Mass
85.solution:
\(\Delta T_f = i K_f m\), with \(\Delta T_f = 0.54\,\text{K}\).

Alkane series: methane (16), ethane (30), propane (44)...

88.solution:
Due to the lanthanoid contraction, ionic radius of M\(^{3+}\) decreases steadily from La to Lu.
La\(^{3+}\) (the first member) has the largest ionic size among Pr, Sm, La and Yb.

89.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
89.solution: The green chemistry principle 'reduce derivatives' recommends minimising or avoiding unnecessary derivatisation (use of protecting/deprotecting groups, blocking groups), since such steps require additional reagents and generate waste.

90.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
90.solution:
Nernst: \(E_{cell} = E^\circ_{cell} - \dfrac{0.0592}{n}\log_{10}\dfrac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]}\).
Since \([\text{Zn}^{2+}] = [\text{Cu}^{2+}] = 0.1\,\text{M}\), the log term is 0.
\(E_{cell} = 1.1\,\text{V} - 0 = 1.1\,\text{V}\).

91.subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
91.solution:
Lattice enthalpy increases with higher ionic charge and smaller ionic size (greater charge density).
\(\text{BeF}_2\) has the smallest, most highly charged cation (Be\(^{2+}\)) and small F\(^-\), giving the highest lattice enthalpy among the options.

92.solution:
Functional isomers have the same molecular formula but different functional groups.
Butan-1-ol (alcohol) and 1-methoxypropane (ether) both have formula \(\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}\) but different functional groups — a pair of functional isomers.

93.subtopic: Nomenclature and Classification of Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
93.solution:
Within a homologous series, boiling point rises with molar mass (more surface area, stronger van der Waals forces).
Among ethanal, propanal, pentanal and hexanal, hexanal (largest) has the highest boiling point.

94.solution:
For a non-volatile, non-electrolyte solute: \(\Delta T_b = K_b\, m\).
\(m = \dfrac{\Delta T_b}{K_b} = \dfrac{1.75}{3} = 0.58\,m\).

95.subtopic: Types of Solids, Crystal Systems and Properties
95.solution:
Isomorphous substances have the same crystal structure and the same atomic ratio of constituents.
\(\text{NaNO}_3\) and \(\text{CaCO}_3\) both have a 1:1:3 atomic ratio and the same (rhombohedral, calcite-type) structure, so they are isomorphous.

97.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
97.solution:
In aqueous medium, basic strength of methylamines follows:
\(\text{NH}_3 < (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N} < \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 < (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}\).
The secondary amine is most basic (best balance of +I effect and solvation), trimethylamine is depressed by steric/solvation factors.

101.solution: For \(n=100\) tosses, \(P(\text{even number of heads}) = \sum_{k \text{ even}} \binom{100}{k}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{100}\).\nUsing \((1+1)^{100} + (1-1)^{100} = 2\sum_{k\text{ even}}\binom{100}{k}\), the sum of even-index binomial coefficients \(= \frac{2^{100}+0}{2} = 2^{99}\).\n\(\therefore P = \frac{2^{99}}{2^{100}} = \frac{1}{2}\).

102.solution: Using the identity \((\overline{a}\times\overline{b})\cdot(\overline{c}\times\overline{d}) = (\overline{a}\cdot\overline{c})(\overline{b}\cdot\overline{d}) - (\overline{a}\cdot\overline{d})(\overline{b}\cdot\overline{c})\), the given determinant equals \((\overline{a}\times\overline{b})\cdot(\overline{c}\times\overline{d}) = 0\).\n\(\therefore (2\widehat{i}+3\widehat{j}-\widehat{k})\cdot(3\widehat{i}+2\widehat{j}+\lambda\widehat{k}) = 0\)\n\(\Rightarrow 6+6-\lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 12\).

104.subtopic: Combined Equation and Condition for Pair of Lines
104.solution:
Bisectors of the coordinate axes have slopes \(1\) and \(-1\).
Line through \((-2,3)\) with slope \(1\): \(x-y+5=0\).
Line through \((-2,3)\) with slope \(-1\): \(x+y-1=0\).
Joint equation: \((x-y+5)(x+y-1) = x^2 - y^2 + 4x + 6y - 5 = 0\).

At \(t=0\), \(T=370\Rightarrow c=\log 80\).\nAt \(t=10\), \(T=330\Rightarrow \log 40 = -10k+\log 80\Rightarrow k = \frac{1}{10}\log 2\).\nAt \(T=295\): \(\log 5 = -\frac{t}{10}\log 2 + \log 80 \Rightarrow \frac{t}{10}\log 2 = \log 16\Rightarrow t = 40\) min.

115.solution: Equation is homogeneous: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y}{x}\left[\log\frac{y}{x}+1\right]\).\nPut \(v=\frac{y}{x}\): \(v+x\frac{dv}{dx} = v(\log v+1)\Rightarrow x\frac{dv}{dx}=v\log v\Rightarrow \frac{dv}{v\log v} = \frac{dx}{x}\).\nIntegrating: \(\log(\log v) = \log x + \log c \Rightarrow \log v = cx\Rightarrow \log\frac{y}{x} = cx\).

116.solution: \(\sqrt{\frac{dy}{dx}} = 4\frac{dy}{dx}+7x\). Squaring removes the radical, giving \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 16\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 56x\frac{dy}{dx}+49x^2\).\nHighest derivative is the first order, raised to power \(2\): order \(=1\), degree \(=2\).

117.solution: Circle touching Y-axis at origin with centre \((h,0)\): \(x^2+y^2 = 2hx\), i.e. \(x^2-2hx+y^2=0\).\nDifferentiating: \(2x-2h+2y\frac{dy}{dx}=0\Rightarrow h = x+y\frac{dy}{dx}\).\nSubstituting back: \(x^2 - 2x\left(x+y\frac{dy}{dx}\right)+y^2 = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 - y^2 + 2xy\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\).
